messages:
maya: hey @sam @chris quick ping — opened PR #812 to change how the streaming client propagates tool-call headers. CI is failing on integration tests, can someone take a quick look? link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/812 :eyes:

sam: taking a look now. which test is blowing up? ci log?

ci-bot: Build failed on integration/test_toolcall.py::test_header_propagation (run #452)
```
E   AssertionError: Expected header 'x-tool-session' in request.headers
```

sam: hmm looks like header merge path may be dropping lower-priority headers when streaming chunks are sent. will repro locally.

chris: fyi i glanced at the pr — the change flattens header dicts into a list and re-applies later. suspect race where chunk-send path calls `make_request()` with only the chunk headers. quick diff that might help:
```py
- headers = {**base_headers, **tool_headers}
+ # ensure base headers are always present even when chunk_headers provided
+ headers = base_headers.copy()
+ headers.update(tool_headers)
```

chris: can someone confirm tests assert on header keys (not order)? tests look brittle.

maya: thanks @chris. test is asserting membership but our fixtures create headers in different places depending on flow. @tina can you run the failing integration locally? might be faster than waiting on CI.

tina: yeah i can spin it up. running `pytest integration/test_toolcall.py::test_header_propagation -q` now. will post output in ~5m.

sam: if chris' change is small i'll push a follow-up commit to the branch, run unit + integration locally before merging. prefer not to rerun the whole CI queue.

ci-bot: New build queued (#453) triggered by push to branch pr/812

ops-deploy-bot: merge window for library changes today closes at 18:00 PST. small fixes can be merged earlier if green and have 1+ approvals.

tina: local run: 
```
collected 1 item
 integration/test_toolcall.py::test_header_propagation PASSED
```

sam: nice. so local passes after chris' patch? did you apply it or the branch already had it?

tina: branch had the original change. i patched `streaming/request.py` locally with chris' ordering fix and re-ran — pass. i also tested with slow chunking (latency emulation) and headers stayed intact.

chris: cool. i'll open a tiny commit to the PR with that change and a one-line comment in the test to assert on `in` rather than equality to avoid order sensitivity.

maya: perfect. once sam verifies CI green can we get one approval then merge? @sam can you be the approver after sanity check?

sam: yep i'll approve after CI passes. if CI is green i'll merge and backport to the 1.3.x branch.

maya: awesome, thanks everyone :tada:
